units.sentence: If the later base-side change is shared among customer groups the way base revenues are today, that ranking holds, ... however much of the change reaches base rates.
units.reason: Checked algebraically: with credit X, pass-through p, fuel share f and base share b, a group's gain relative to its bill is X(f - p*b)/(F*f + B*b), which rises with f/b for any p >= 0 (derivative numerator B + F*p > 0). So groups with f/b > 1 (medium 1.14, large 1.59, agricultural 1.32, government 1.62) stay ahead of those with f/b < 1 (domestic 0.95, small business 0.75, lighting 0.60) at any pass-through; carrying cost only scales p. Unstated assumptions: the fuel-side saving follows P-116's fuel-revenue shares, and 'today' means the 2023 test-year study GAM cites.

units.sentence: On that condition, and with no added carrying cost, homes as a group come out ahead in dollars unless about 95% or more of the base-side change reaches base rates.
Georgia Power's per-$100 million examples follow its storm-cost and fuel-rate changes; by those examples, a typical home comes out ahead unless about 90% or more of the change reaches base rates.
units.reason: 1.48058 / 1.64844 = 0.898, about 90%; inputs match P-142 (-1.4805840) and P-143 (1.6484420); 'storm-cost and fuel-rate changes' matches P-141. The previous sentence's 'no added carrying cost' isn't restated (minor).

framing_issues.text: no filing we read gives a home's net or the fuel-charge date
framing_issues.issue: 'net' is undefined jargon for a phone reader (net of what?), and 'the fuel-charge date' is vague. Same on L15 ('a business's net'). Suggest 'the overall effect on a home's bill' and 'when the fuel charge would change'.

framing_issues.text: Any baseline power you have is billed at standard rates, so the lines above apply.
framing_issues.issue: Vague reference: 'the lines above' (the home line or the business line?). Suggest 'so the standard-rate lines above apply to that part'.

framing_issues.text: Size and timing aren't known as of Nov 8, 2026, as above.
framing_issues.issue: Vague reference ('Size and timing' of what?) and unscoped ('aren't known'), unlike the scoped lines it points to.

framing_issues.text: As of Nov 8, 2026, no filing we read gives any effect on your bill or its timing.
framing_issues.issue: Right after saying this case doesn't set EMC or city-utility rates, this hints that some effect exists but is unmeasured. Suggest 'No filing we read says this case would change your bill.'

framing_issues.text: would add about $126 million to the fuel credit in 2026
framing_issues.issue: The 2026 figure is Staff's projection for a year that ends two weeks after the Dec 15 decision; readers may take it as money reaching 2026 bills. Suggest 'Staff's projections: about $126 million for 2026, rising to about $399 million in 2031'.

framing_issues.text: Dec 14 at 9:30 a.m. is the earliest possible cutoff
framing_issues.issue: Deadline advice stated with more certainty than the sources allow: the case also goes to the Dec 10 Energy Committee meeting (P-012), and no passage says whether that counts as 'a Commission vote' (P-030).

framing_issues.text: We found no ruling on that request in the case's filing list as of Nov 8.
framing_issues.issue: Date lacks the year; the project writes absolute dates and other changed lines say 'Nov 8, 2026'.

framing_issues.text: Each plan would raise the fuel credit
framing_issues.issue: 'Each plan' can be read to include Plan A (today's method), which would not raise the credit. Suggest 'Each of these three plans'.

framing_issues.text: GAM's witness, who warns about a bigger fuel credit, said
framing_issues.issue: Verb chosen only for GAM ('warns', also L159 'warns of upward pressure'); other parties 'said' or 'asked'. Mildly dramatizing; suggest 'who says a bigger fuel credit would raise pressure on base rates'.

framing_issues.text: If you care most about keeping the real-time rate's design intact
framing_issues.issue: L16 tells real-time customers the case is not about their hourly prices, yet this value line is about keeping the rate's 'design' intact; without a gloss (Georgia Power means keeping the credit tied to marginal cost, P-121, P-129) readers may be confused about what is at stake.

framing_issues.text: Today's method, Plan A, has no line: no party whose testimony we could read backs it in every part.
framing_issues.issue: Structural balance: Plan A gets no values line and readers are told no one backs it, while GAM's line (keeping base rates down) is in effect the case for it and GAM accepts a change only 'Should the Commission find' one is needed (P-111). Can leave Plan A without its strongest case.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power also says it is committed to protecting existing customers from the costs of adding large customers.
framing_issues.issue: Unequal treatment: Georgia Power gets a second statement in the values section, placed right after GIPL's 'protecting customers on standard rates' line, where it reads as a rebuttal; no other party gets a second line. Move it to Plan B or drop it.

framing_issues.text: that leaves no extra money to push rates down
framing_issues.issue: Paraphrase drops GIPL's qualifier 'from an economics perspective' (P-098), making the claim sound more absolute.

framing_issues.text: Take-or-pay choice 1 would count more real-time money toward fuel, which lowers the fuel charge.
framing_issues.issue: Certainty differs from the rest of the page ('would likely'), and from Plans C and D, which carry no such clause.

framing_issues.text: PIA Staff had said its take-or-pay choice "is consistent with the 2010 rate case proposal."
framing_issues.issue: The Georgia Power point this answers (choice 2 is 'a departure' from the 2010 approach, P-129) isn't in this bullet, and '2010 rate case proposal' is unexplained here.

framing_issues.text: Georgia Power offered two take-or-pay choices, take-or-pay choices 1 and 2
framing_issues.issue: Redundant wording (also L171 'two other choices ..., take-or-pay choices 1 and 2'); suggest 'two take-or-pay choices, 1 and 2, which the filings call Option 1 and Option 2'.

framing_issues.text: GIPL says real-time load should bear costs of plants run in response to it
framing_issues.issue: 'it' is a vague reference, and 'plants' narrows GIPL's 'resources' (P-100), which can include purchases.

framing_issues.text: offered take-or-pay choice 2 as one of its two fixes
framing_issues.issue: 'fixes' presumes a problem Georgia Power framed as 'their concern' (P-058: 'two potential options to address their concern'). Suggest 'options'.

framing_issues.text: How the two options compare in size, since only take-or-pay choice 2 has a public estimate.
framing_issues.issue: Mixed terms in one sentence ('options' and 'take-or-pay choice'); L250 says 'both options', and the nocheck labels on L231 and L243 still say 'Option 1/2' while their headings say 'take-or-pay choice'.

framing_issues.text: real-time money keeps lowering base costs
framing_issues.issue: Stated as fact in GAM's card, while card 8's In short attributes a similar base-side claim to Georgia Power; it rests on GAM (P-111) and Georgia Power (P-124), and GIPL says the idea 'neglects two critical factors' (P-099). Suggest 'GAM says real-time money keeps lowering base costs'.

framing_issues.text: "Plan C": {text: "PSC staff's plan"}
framing_issues.issue: Can read as the regulator's own plan; PIA Staff is a party separate from the advisory staff that counsels the commissioners (P-006, P-007). The other chips name a party ('Georgia Power's plan', 'Interfaith group's plan').

framing_issues.text: link_text: "Larger businesses' real-time power payments and your fuel charge"
framing_issues.issue: Names only the fuel charge (the side that would likely fall); the title and 30-second version also name base costs. Consider '...and your power bill'.

framing_issues.text: S10: Filing page
framing_issues.issue: Only source label that doesn't name its party (Resource Supply Management); 'Filing page' tells the reader nothing about whose filing it is.
